summary: This week's Gulf technology, finance, and regulatory developments underline a deepening institutional commitment to regional economic integration, cross-border payment harmonization, and targeted artificial intelligence deployments. Most notably, GCC remittances reached a record $161 billion in 2025, surging 13.6%, reflecting robust labor markets and capital flows across the bloc. Monetary and payment frameworks saw significant diplomatic and institutional activity, with the central banks of the UAE and Syria agreeing on payment and monetary policy cooperation, while the UAE and Morocco explored linking instant payment systems alongside signed memoranda of understanding. Concurrently, capital markets and strategic infrastructure continued to scale; Oman’s OQ Gas Networks launched a $1 billion sukuk programme, and Qatar issued Government Ijara Sukuk worth QR 4.1 billion. In the digital and government technology spheres, state-backed entities accelerated applied AI initiatives—exemplified by Kuwait Oil Company deploying its 'Sanad' AI platform to operationalize drilling knowledge, and UAE researchers advancing AI applications in healthcare and oncology. Furthermore, digital government expansion gathered pace, highlighted by Dubai CommerCity launching an AED 1.8 billion expansion and Qatar’s MCIT partnering with PwC Middle East. For C-suite and board leaders across GCC banking and gov-tech organizations, these trends signal an increasingly interconnected operational environment requiring robust cross-border compliance, modernized payment rails, and disciplined scaling of proprietary AI use cases.

stories.t: GCC remittances hit record $161 billion in 2025
stories.b: GCC remittances surged by 13.6% to reach a record $161 billion in 2025, according to a Zawya report. The milestone underscores the continued strength of expatriate labor markets and financial flows across member states.
stories.w: Provides macro-level liquidity insights and highlights high-volume corridor opportunities for regional retail banks and digital remittance providers.

stories.t: CBUAE and Bank Al-Maghrib sign bilateral MoUs
stories.b: The Central Bank of the UAE and Bank Al-Maghrib have signed two memoranda of understanding to strengthen institutional ties. The agreement complements broader North African financial cooperation initiatives.
stories.w: Opens formal bilateral channels for regulatory alignment and potential future cross-border financial market connectivity between the UAE and Morocco.

stories.t: UAE and Morocco central banks explore linking instant payment systems
stories.b: Central banking authorities from the UAE and Morocco have initiated discussions to explore the technical and regulatory framework required to link their instant payment systems.
stories.w: Signals a clear strategic push toward bilateral real-time gross settlement and instant payment interoperability across non-GCC Arab trade corridors.

stories.t: Oman’s OQ Gas Networks launches $1 billion sukuk programme
stories.b: OQ Gas Networks has officially launched a $1 billion sukuk programme, offering a major new debt instrument originating from Oman. The issuance aims to fund strategic energy infrastructure and optimize capital structures.
stories.w: Expands regional fixed-income depth and offers institutional investors a large-scale, infrastructure-backed Islamic finance asset in Oman.

stories.t: QCB issues Government Ijara Sukuk worth QR 4.1 billion
stories.b: The Qatar Central Bank has issued Government Ijara Sukuk valued at QR 4.1 billion. The domestic issuance supports local liquidity management and Islamic debt market benchmark development.
stories.w: Provides Qatari financial institutions with high-quality liquid assets (HQLA) compliant with Sharia liquidity requirements.

stories.t: KOC deploys 'Sanad' AI to unlock institutional drilling knowledge
stories.b: Kuwait Oil Company (KOC) has introduced 'Sanad', an artificial intelligence tool designed to capture and deploy decades of technical drilling know-how directly to engineers.
stories.w: Demonstrates enterprise-grade domain-specific AI adoption in heavy industry, serving as a benchmark for operational efficiency in hydrocarbon sectors.

stories.t: Dubai CommerCity launches AED 1.8 billion expansion
stories.b: Dubai CommerCity has initiated an AED 1.8 billion expansion project aimed at scaling infrastructure for future commerce and accelerating the emirate's digital economy growth.
stories.w: Reinforces Dubai’s commercial real estate and e-commerce infrastructure capacity, creating new opportunities for digital-native merchants and logistics tech firms.

stories.t: Qatar's MCIT partners with PwC Middle East for digital government
stories.b: Qatar's Ministry of Communications and Information Technology (MCIT) has signed a Memorandum of Understanding with PwC Middle East to advance national digital government development initiatives.
stories.w: Leverages strategic advisory partnerships to accelerate public sector digital transformation roadmaps and e-government service delivery.

stories.t: UAE introduces new WPS salary payment rules for employers
stories.b: The UAE has issued detailed guidelines explaining a new Wages Protection System (WPS) process designed to tighten employer compliance and safeguard worker wage disbursements.
stories.w: Requires regional employers and payroll processors to update compliance workflows and system interfaces to avoid regulatory penalties.

stories.t: Kuwait enacts new media law to regulate social media ads
stories.b: Kuwait has implemented a new media law that formally brings social media advertising under regulatory oversight, imposing clearer compliance frameworks on commercial digital promotion.
stories.w: Affects digital marketing budgets, influencer operations, and corporate social media compliance standards across Kuwaiti digital channels.

themes.t: Cross-Border Payment Linkages and Central Bank Diplomacy
themes.b: Regional central banks are actively pursuing bilateral cooperation agreements and technical links to integrate cross-border payments. The UAE's recent central banking agreements with Syria and Morocco, alongside a broader surge in GCC remittances to $161 billion, highlight an intensified focus on friction-free, secure financial corridors.

themes.t: Applied Enterprise AI and Specialized Knowledge Management
themes.b: Gulf organizations are shifting from high-level AI experimentation to embedding domain-specific applications into heavy industry workflows. Kuwait Oil Company's deployment of the 'Sanad' AI platform and UAE initiatives in digital health and drug discovery demonstrate a pragmatic drive toward operational efficiency.

themes.t: Islamic Capital Market Expansion and Infrastructure Financing
themes.b: Large-scale debt issuances and sovereign sukuk programs are driving liquidity management across the Gulf. Significant activities—such as Oman's OQ Gas Networks $1 billion sukuk programme and Qatar Central Bank's QR 4.1 billion Ijara Sukuk issuance—provide deep institutional assets and fund vital infrastructural growth.

items: Evaluate cloud and on-premise infrastructure readiness to support domain-specific AI knowledge management systems inspired by KOC's 'Sanad' model.
Assess enterprise architecture scalability to integrate upcoming cross-border instant payment linkages driven by regional central bank initiatives.
Audit current digital commerce and portal infrastructures in light of major logistics and e-commerce real estate expansions like Dubai CommerCity.
Review and harden cybersecurity protocols in partnership with national cyber councils, echoing recent UAE cybersecurity public-private alignments.
Ensure robust encryption and data residency controls for proprietary engineering and operational data utilized by enterprise AI assistants.
Monitor regulatory updates stemming from new digital advertising and media compliance laws in regional markets such as Kuwait.
Establish data curation pipelines to convert institutional tacit knowledge into structured, searchable corpuses for enterprise AI consumption.
Standardize cross-border data governance frameworks to comply with evolving central bank monetary and payment integration agreements.
Enhance data quality frameworks supporting automated payroll and regulatory reporting systems under updated regional labor rules.
Align organizational transformation roadmaps with national digital government frameworks, leveraging strategic consulting partnerships like Qatar's MCIT-PwC initiative.
Incorporate upgraded wage protection and regulatory compliance workflows into enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems.
Capitalize on favorable regional liquidity and sukuk market developments to optimize capital allocation for digital transformation projects.

market.b: Remittance volumes reached historic highs at $161 billion in 2025, while central banks actively pursued instant payment system linkages across North Africa and the Levant.
Debt capital markets experienced robust activity with major sovereign and corporate sukuk issuances from Oman and Qatar, supported by strong institutional liquidity.
Enterprise AI adoption matured into specialized operational tools, highlighted by proprietary industrial knowledge platforms and advanced healthcare applications.
Public sector digitalization accelerated through strategic advisory partnerships and massive commercial infrastructure expansions designed to foster digital economies.

ceo.lead: If I were advising the CEO of a Gulf bank or government technology organisation, the three issues I would put on the leadership agenda this week are...
items: Capitalizing on Cross-Border Payment Integration: Formulating a strategic response to ongoing central bank initiatives linking regional instant payment systems to capture shifting remittance and trade corridors.

Scaling Pragmatic, Proprietary AI Solutions: Moving beyond generative AI hype to evaluate domain-specific enterprise deployments—similar to industrial knowledge-sharing platforms—that protect proprietary data while driving measurable efficiency.

Navigating Evolving Regulatory Compliance: Ensuring internal governance, payroll, and digital marketing frameworks fully adapt to tightening local regulations, such as Kuwait's new media laws and updated WPS compliance rules.
